amendments.normalized_body: In `legacy_process_param_normalization` (crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1192), the `_unit` parameter is accepted but completely ignored — normalization is purely name-based. This means if a developer attaches param_meta to `aob_k_tan_mg` with `unit = "mg total"` instead of `unit = "mg N/L"`, the system will still normalize the value to a concentration, creating a mismatch between the stated unit and the displayed value. Consider either (a) removing the unused `_unit` parameter to avoid implying it influences behavior, or (b) adding a debug assertion or warning when the attached unit doesn't match the expected normalization target (e.g., warn if a `_mg` legacy field has `unit` set to something other than a per-liter concentration).

Finish the kinetic-field rename consistently across the data/scenario codepaths. `ProcessParamsPreset` now defines canonical `*_mg_c_per_l` / `*_mg_n_per_l` / `*_mg_per_l` fields in `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:760-801`, but validation/tests still dereference removed names in `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1565-1579` and `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:2339`, and scenario materialization still reads the removed fields in `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:367-386`. The branch does not build: `cargo test -p tank_data -q` and `cargo test -p tank_scenarios -q` both fail with `E0609` on these lines.

Restore a real migration path for legacy kinetic `_mg` process keys instead of treating them as raw mg/L aliases. The runtime/data structs now only add `serde(alias = "..._mg")` for `decomposer_*`, `aob_*`, `nob_*`, and `comammox_*` in `crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:59-111` and `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:763-801`, while `parse_process_params_preset()` only renormalizes the plant/algae `*_mg_total` keys in `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1186-1291`. `legacy_process_param_normalization()` no longer returns `LegacyMgPerL` for any renamed kinetic parameter in `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1345-1365`, so a legacy file such as `aob_k_tan_mg = 0.5` is now interpreted as `0.5 mg N/L` instead of the previous `0.025 mg N/L`. The still-stale regression in `crates/tank_data/src/lib.rs:316-335` expecting `aob_k_tan_mg = 200.0` to report `value 10` shows the old 20 L compatibility contract was intended to remain intact.
